title: Stage presentation with large projection screen showing 'The World of Future Tomorrow'

A large projection screen occupies the full rear of the stage and displays a colorful infographic.
One grand piano is visible on the right side of the stage (viewer right).
One drum kit (drum set) is positioned center stage in front of the projection screen.
At least three guitar amplifiers or speaker cabinets are visible left-of-center on the stage in front of the screen (they appear side-by-side; some are partially obscured).
Two floor monitor speakers are visible on the front edge of the stage: one left front and one right front (the right-front monitor is partly cropped by the image edge).
A row of stackable chairs is visible on the viewer-right side of the stage (at least six individual chairs can be distinguished).
A small number of handheld cameras or mobile devices are visible at the very bottom edge of the image (two devices or heads are partially visible and cropped by the image edge).

The grand piano is located to the viewer-right of the drum kit and slightly behind the speaker.
The amplifiers/speaker cabinets are positioned to the viewer-left of the drum kit in a cluster near the screen.
Two floor monitors sit on the stage floor at the front edge, roughly left-front and right-front relative to the stage.
A line of chairs is arranged along the viewer-right side of the stage, behind the piano and toward the screen.
Instrument stands and cable runs are concentrated around the drum kit and amplifiers, crossing the stage floor toward the front monitors.

The stage floor is light brown wood (visible planks) with a polished appearance.
The grand piano and most electronic equipment (amplifiers, monitors, drum hardware) are black.
The projection text 'The World of Future Tomorrow' is yellow.
The amplifiers and many cables appear black or dark coloured; chairs on the right are dark (black or dark grey).
An instrument with a gilded or carved wooden frame (gold/brown) is visible left-front on the stage.

Some objects at the extreme left and bottom edges of the image are cropped and only partially visible (including audience devices and possibly additional instruments), so their full identity and counts cannot be determined.
